seo_title: Delhi HC Blocks Intas in Helsinn Nausea Drug Suit
title: Delhi HC Grants Helsinn an Ad-Interim Injunction Against Intas's Anti-Nausea Combipack
case_name: Helsinn Healthcare SA & Anr. v. Intas Pharmaceuticals Limited
card_summary: Helsinn Healthcare sued Intas after learning it was launching 'NO-CINV', a combipack of netupitant and palonosetron for chemotherapy-induced nausea. Justice Manmeet Pritam Singh Arora found a prima facie case of patent infringement, uncontested by Intas at the hearing, and granted an ad-interim injunction against the product's manufacture, marketing and sale.
card_tip: A product not contested as infringing at the first hearing usually draws an ad-interim injunction; a defendant wanting to keep selling pending trial needs its non-infringement case ready from day one.
verification_notes: The parties, the product name 'NO-CINV', its composition (netupitant 300 mg plus palonosetron 0.5 mg), the judge (Justice Manmeet Pritam Singh Arora), the finding of uncontested prima facie infringement and the ad-interim injunction are reported consistently by LiveLaw Biz and SupremeToday, both filed within days of the order. The case number, CS(COMM) 1219/2026, is taken from LiveLaw Biz's report. The exact date the order was signed could not be pinned down from either secondary report; LiveLaw Biz's own PDF copy of the order carries a Delhi High Court server download timestamp of 11 November 2026, which is used here as the decision date, flagged as an estimate rather than a confirmed pronouncement date. The order itself was seen only as a server-downloaded copy referenced by LiveLaw Biz, not independently opened and read in full. This is an interim order; the suit remains pending and the position may change at the next hearing.
